research_question: Can the highest-priority Mendes lead be bound to a real catalogued papyrus object and a scholarly textual witness without claiming more than the evidence supports?

object_identity_receipt.dating: 26th Dynasty; palaeographic dating under Psamtik I
object_identity_receipt.content_scope: Religious festivals and mythological/geographical material for Lower Egyptian sites including Mendes

provenance_caution.summary: The Elephantine project metadata lists an ancient provenance assignment to Elephantine with high certainty at database level, while simultaneously noting that the actual find/purchase location is unknown and that the papyrus is devoted to Delta festivals. Therefore JANUS does not treat the physical findspot as securely excavated Mendes or even securely excavated Elephantine.

mendes_textual_receipt.content_paraphrase: For Mendesian Osiris, the passage states that he fecundates as a copulating ba; the divine flesh called the Living is identified with the virile member and the spine/back.

geographic_receipt.local_deity_context: Banebdjedet; UCL records the four souls immanent in Banebdjedet as Ra, Shu, Geb and Osiris.

important_new_inference.statement: The strongest current lead is not a recoverable piece of flesh but a named textual-theological relic tradition centered on Mendes, in which phallus and spine/back form a linked Osirian generative complex.
important_new_inference.not_a_claim: This does not establish that a physical biological phallus was ever stored at Mendes or survives there now.

requirements: Obtain a directly inspectable image/facsimile or licensed scholarly transcription of the relevant Brooklyn XI,10-11 passage.
Extract the Dendera roof-chapel primary hieroglyphic passages that assign phallus relic-simulacra, body-part pairings and reliquary forms to nomes.
Resolve the Upper Egyptian nome 7 Kenem phallus-and-testicles tradition to a secure toponym/site before any archaeological ranking.
Keep Mendes fish-standard/Hatmehyt material as a separate control from Plutarch's phallus-consuming fish list.
